answer: Proof-of-burn resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to destroy native tokens at a provably unspendable address to anchor its public key on-chain. Unlike refundable collateral, this sacrifice leaves only a cryptographic ember etched into a marble ledger, forcing an attacker to incur an irreversible capital cost per fake identity rather than recycling funds. However, wealthy adversaries can still buy multiple identities, pricing out resource-constrained legitimate agents.
